title: Falling ball

slow_motion.evidence: No narration, captions, or on-screen text indicate slow motion; motion appears in real time.

subjects.description: small orange spherical ball falling vertically

observation.what_happens: An orange ball drops vertically from just below a black-and-white scale bar down to a brown floor. The free fall starts at release at the top and ends when the ball first contacts the floor.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself: 3275 px/s² over 8 arcs = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: y repeatedly falls to about -1.43 m then rebounds to decaying heights while x grows steadily, showing a bouncing ball with constant horizontal drift, not a single fall. Restitution looks near 0.7 from successive peak heights. Candidates keep gravity fixed and a floor bounce event, and compete vacuum vs linear vs quadratic air drag with bounce friction to explain later small bounces.

law.title: Vacuum ballistic with bounce
law.summary: A ball flies under gravity alone and bounces off the floor losing the same fraction of speed each time.

fitted.title: Vacuum ballistic with bounce
fitted.summary: A ball flies under gravity alone and bounces off the floor losing the same fraction of speed each time.

candidates.ifItWins: The flight and rebounds are ballistic with no measurable air drag; only gravity and a constant restitution explain the unseen bounces.

law.title: Linear air drag with bounce
law.summary: Same as bouncing ball but air slows it with a force proportional to speed.

fitted.title: Linear air drag with bounce
fitted.summary: Same as bouncing ball but air slows it with a force proportional to speed.

candidates.ifItWins: Air exerts a viscous-like force proportional to velocity in addition to gravity and bounce loss.

law.title: Textbook projectile (no air)
law.summary: Moves at constant horizontal speed while gravity pulls it down at a constant rate.

law.title: Quadratic air drag with frictional bounce
law.summary: A bouncing ball with air resistance that grows as speed squared plus friction that slows sideways motion at each bounce.

fitted.title: Quadratic air drag with frictional bounce
fitted.summary: A bouncing ball with air resistance that grows as speed squared plus friction that slows sideways motion at each bounce.

params.name: cal
params.meaning: scale correction: true metres per provisional metre

candidates.ifItWins: Air drag grows as speed squared and the bounce also scrubs horizontal speed, needed to predict later low bounces and x drift.

caveats: Tracking covers only release to first floor contact, so later bounces are untested.
Horizontal motion is tiny and near measurement noise, so sideways drift is not meaningful.
critique.finding: The ball falls freely under gravity {g} down to floor level {y_floor}. On hitting it bounces up with springiness {e}.
critique.headline: Orange ball falls freely and bounces on floor
critique.why_it_won: The winner captures the fall and the bounce cleanly while showing air drag adds nothing useful.

headline: Orange ball falls freely and bounces on floor
finding: The ball falls freely under gravity 9.81 m/s² down to floor level -1.44 ± 0.0013 m. On hitting it bounces up with springiness 0.72 ± 3.05e-4.

eyeball.law_in_words: ball falls under gravity with strong drag to low terminal speed and hits floor plastically with essentially zero normal rebound velocity
